title: Lewis County Historical Museum

services.name: Featured Exhibit
services.desc: “Sometimes, you just have to clear your head and get out to see other things. It is very important to be nourished. I love to go to museums and galleries - anything creative. It doesn’t promise you inspiration, but it nourishes your creative soul” - Marc Jacobs Features history from both the Upper and Lower Chehalis Tribes and the Cowlitz Tribe. A display is devoted to Mary Kiona (1855?-1970), niece of Cowlitz Chief Scanawa. At the age of 6, she began weaving the intricate cedar root baskets of her tribe. The museum features some of her baskets, which she continued weaving until her death. In her lifetime, she saw the coming of steamboats, trains, automobiles, and jet planes. Roy I. Wilson,

blurb: The Lewis County Historical Society and Museum celebrates the storied history of Lewis County, Washington. Founded on December 21, 1845, Lewis County once stretched at one point from the Cowlitz River to the south and north to Sitka, Alaska.
